stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They hypothesized that the facial expression produced by holding a pen would affect amusement.

**Participants.** The sample was 90 university students, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

**Results.** The group that held the pen between the teeth: mean funniness rating (1 to 10) = 6.6. The group that held the pen between the lips: mean funniness rating (1 to 10) = 5.1. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?**

**Source A.** In a study of 350 adults, the number of stressful life events in the past year correlated with the number of colds in that year (r = +0.33). Adults who reported sleeping less tended to report both more stress and more colds.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 84 office workers were randomly assigned to practice mindfulness meditation or to listen to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day. After eight weeks, the meditation group had a mean cortisol level of 9.8 nmol/L and the audiobook group 13.5 nmol/L (p = 0.02).

**Source C.** Researchers followed 500 people for a year after a major flood. Those who reported strong support from family and friends had fewer symptoms of illness and depression than those who reported little support.

questions.stem: Each fishing boat catches as many fish as it can, and soon the fish stocks collapse for all the boats. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.
The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.
Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.
Correct. A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.explanation: A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.stem: Positive psychologists group bravery, perseverance and honesty under which virtue?

options.why: Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.
Correct. Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.
Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.explanation: Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a schema?

options.text: The interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema
options.why: That describes assimilation.

options.text: The changing of an existing schema to fit new information
options.why: That describes accommodation.

options.text: A mental framework that organizes and interprets information
options.why: Correct. This is what a schema means.

options.text: The best or most typical example of a category
options.why: That describes a prototype.

questions.explanation: A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes interposition?

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer
options.why: Correct. This is what interposition means.

options.text: The binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object
options.why: That describes convergence.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance
options.why: That describes linear perspective.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away
options.why: That describes texture gradient.

questions.explanation: Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.

questions.stem: A study tested only male university students, so critics doubt that its findings apply to older adults or to women. Which quality of the study are they questioning?

options.why: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.
Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.
Correct. Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.
A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.

questions.explanation: Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress?

options.why: Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Correct. Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.

questions.explanation: Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a reuptake inhibitor?

options.text: A drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption
options.why: Correct. This is what a reuptake inhibitor means.

options.text: The need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use
options.why: That describes tolerance.

options.text: The unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug
options.why: That describes withdrawal.

options.text: A drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it
options.why: That describes an agonist.

questions.explanation: A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels?

options.why: Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.
The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.
Correct. The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.

questions.explanation: The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to remember the last items in a list well?

options.why: Correct. The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.
The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.explanation: The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.

questions.stem: At seventy, Mr. Park does better at crossword puzzles and vocabulary tests than he did at thirty. Which kind of intelligence does this show?

options.why: Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Correct. Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.
The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.

questions.explanation: Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the expectation that people will help those who have helped them?

options.why: Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
Correct. The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.
The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.

questions.explanation: The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.stem: Carl's behavior is far outside what people in his culture consider usual or acceptable. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.
Correct. Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.
Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.

questions.explanation: Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress?

options.why: Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.
Correct. Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.
Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.

questions.stem: After spinning on a ride, Zoe feels dizzy because the fluid in her inner ear is still moving. Which sense is affected?

options.why: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
Correct. The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.explanation: The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.stem: Researchers find that adults who suffered abuse and neglect as children have higher rates of illness and depression. These early events are called which of the following?

options.why: The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.
Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.
Correct. Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.

questions.explanation: Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences?

options.why: Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.
Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.
Correct. Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.

questions.explanation: Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period?

options.why: Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.
Correct. Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.explanation: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.stem: After solving ten math problems with one formula, Abby keeps trying that formula on a problem that needs a different approach. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Convergent thinking is thinking that narrows the possibilities down to the single best answer.
Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.
Correct. A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.
Functional fixedness is the inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose.

questions.explanation: A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.

questions.stem: In a town where most people earn modest incomes and a few earn millions, the mean income is far above the median. Which shape does the distribution have?

options.why: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of scores.
Correct. A positive skew is a distribution with a few extremely high scores, which pull the mean above the median.
The mode is the score that occurs most often.
A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.explanation: A positive skew is a distribution with a few extremely high scores, which pull the mean above the median.

questions.stem: In the early 1900s, some officials used test scores to justify laws that prevented certain people from having children. This is an example of which of the following?

options.why: Nature is the influence of inherited genetic factors on behavior and mental processes.
A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.
The evolutionary perspective is the approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce.
Correct. Eugenics is the discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans.

questions.explanation: Eugenics is the discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes subjective well-being?

options.text: The positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person
options.why: That describes signature strengths.

options.text: The appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being
options.why: That describes gratitude.

options.text: The positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event
options.why: That describes posttraumatic growth.

options.text: A person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life
options.why: Correct. This is what subjective well-being means.

questions.explanation: Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others?

options.why: Correct. Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.
Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.

questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.

questions.stem: Yara loves trying unfamiliar foods, visiting art galleries and exploring new ideas. She would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Correct. Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.

questions.explanation: Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: A researcher asks how much of a child's musical ability comes from genes and how much from lessons. Which theme of developmental psychology is this?

options.why: Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.
Discontinuous development is the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase.
Correct. Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.
A longitudinal study is research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period.

questions.explanation: Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: Score on a timed reasoning test
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of years since leaving school
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes projection?

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: That describes rationalization.

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: Correct. This is what projection means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: That describes denial.

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: That describes displacement.

questions.explanation: Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.

questions.stem: A researcher claims that dreams help move the day's experiences into long-term storage. Which theory of dreaming is this?

options.why: Correct. The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.
Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.explanation: The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events?

options.why: The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.
Correct. The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.

questions.explanation: The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes flat affect?

options.text: A false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it
options.why: That describes a delusion.

options.text: The jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia
options.why: That describes disorganized speech.

options.text: A lack of emotional expression in the face and voice
options.why: Correct. This is what flat affect means.

options.text: A sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus
options.why: That describes a hallucination.

questions.explanation: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles?

options.why: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Correct. Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.

questions.explanation: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.stem: A second laboratory repeats a famous memory study with new participants to check the result. This is an example of which of the following?

options.why: An operational definition is a statement of exactly how a variable is measured or manipulated in a study.
A hypothesis is a testable prediction about the relationship between variables.
Correct. Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.
An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.

questions.explanation: Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Of two identical twins with the same genetic risk for schizophrenia, only the one who lived through severe trauma develops it. Which model best explains this?

options.why: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.
The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
Correct. The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.
Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.

questions.explanation: The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
Debriefing happens after the study.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: During adolescence, the reproductive organs themselves mature. These organs are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.
Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.

questions.explanation: Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses?

options.why: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Correct. Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.explanation: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions?

options.why: Correct. A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.
An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.

questions.explanation: A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.

questions.stem: A man giving directions does not notice that the stranger he is talking to was swapped for a different person when a door passed between them. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.
Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
Correct. Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.

questions.explanation: Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.

questions.stem: Immediately after firing, a neuron cannot fire again until it has reset. What is this pause called?

options.why: The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.
Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.
The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.
Correct. The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.explanation: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: The group that waited with four other people
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes source amnesia?

options.text: The distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event
options.why: That describes the misinformation effect.

options.text: The building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information
options.why: That describes constructive memory.

options.text: The increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it
options.why: That describes imagination inflation.

options.text: The inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned
options.why: Correct. This is what source amnesia means.

questions.explanation: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.stem: A group of people who mildly support a policy discuss it together and end up strongly supporting it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.
Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Correct. Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.

questions.explanation: Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes rods?

options.text: The point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells
options.why: That describes the blind spot.

options.text: The receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light
options.why: That describes cones.

options.text: The receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision
options.why: Correct. This is what rods means.

options.text: The central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest
options.why: That describes the fovea.

questions.explanation: Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an internal locus of control?

options.text: The tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly
options.why: That describes the mere exposure effect.

options.text: An expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true
options.why: That describes a self-fulfilling prophecy.

options.text: The belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions
options.why: Correct. This is what an internal locus of control means.

options.text: An explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances
options.why: That describes a situational attribution.

questions.explanation: An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes REM sleep?

options.text: The sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles
options.why: Correct. This is what REM sleep means.

options.text: The brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling
options.why: That describes NREM stage 1.

options.text: The body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep
options.why: That describes the circadian rhythm.

options.text: The deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake
options.why: That describes NREM stage 3.

questions.explanation: REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.

questions.stem: In psychodynamic theory, denial, projection and rationalization are all examples of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.

questions.explanation: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: Conscientiousness score on a personality inventory
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: The number of hours worked in a paid job
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: After the study behind his favorite diet is shown to be fraudulent, Raj still insists that the diet works. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.

questions.explanation: Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression?

options.why: Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.
Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Correct. Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.

questions.explanation: Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.

questions.stem: In Pavlov's experiments, dogs salivated to food, and later to a tone that had been paired with food. Salivating to the tone alone was which of the following?

options.why: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
Correct. The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.

questions.explanation: The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.

questions.stem: For most people, speech is controlled mainly by the left hemisphere, while recognizing faces relies more on the right. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Correct. Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.

questions.explanation: Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The warmth of parenting, as rated by observers
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The level of financial stress in the family
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Critics argue that a so-called creativity test actually measures vocabulary. Which quality are they questioning?

options.why: Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.
Correct. Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.

questions.explanation: Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a lobotomy?

options.text: The treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression
options.why: That describes transcranial magnetic stimulation.

options.text: The now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain
options.why: Correct. This is what a lobotomy means.

options.text: Any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder
options.why: That describes psychotropic medication.

options.text: The treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient
options.why: That describes electroconvulsive therapy.

questions.explanation: A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.stem: A hearing test finds the quietest tone that Aiko can detect on 50 percent of trials. What does this test measure?

options.why: Correct. The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.
Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.
Synesthesia is the condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense.
The just-noticeable difference is the smallest difference between two stimuli that a person can detect half of the time.

questions.explanation: The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.93, −0.44, −0.35, +0.28. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: +0.28 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.93 is farthest from zero.
−0.44 is closer to zero.
−0.35 is closer to zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.93 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: A baby whose cries are answered with food and comfort learns that the world is dependable. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.
Correct. Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.

questions.explanation: Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is?

options.why: Correct. Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.
The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.
Statistical significance is the conclusion that a result is unlikely to have occurred by chance, usually when p is below 0.05.
A confounding variable is a factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results.

questions.explanation: Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.

questions.stem: As well as obtaining permission from the parents, the researchers asked each child whether he or she was willing to take part. What is the child's agreement called?

options.why: Correct. Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.
Deception is misleading participants about the study.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Confidentiality is keeping data private.

questions.explanation: Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.

questions.stem: An exam, a traffic jam and an argument each set off a stress reaction. Each of these events is which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A stressor is an event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging.
The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.
Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.
The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.

questions.explanation: A stressor is an event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Consent is obtained before the study.
Replication is repeating a study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: Taking a tablet makes Lena's headache go away, so she is more likely to take a tablet next time. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes phonemic encoding?

options.text: The shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance
options.why: That describes structural encoding.

options.text: The encoding of a word based on its sound
options.why: Correct. This is what phonemic encoding means.

options.text: The memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall
options.why: That describes implicit memory.

options.text: The encoding that requires attention and conscious effort
options.why: That describes effortful processing.

questions.explanation: Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: The night before a test, Gia studies for six hours without a break. Which kind of practice is she using?

options.why: A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.
A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.
Correct. Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.

questions.explanation: Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes gender identity?

options.text: A person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination
options.why: Correct. This is what gender identity means.

options.text: The direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction
options.why: That describes sexual orientation.

options.text: The socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman
options.why: That describes gender.

options.text: The set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women
options.why: That describes a gender role.

questions.explanation: Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.

questions.stem: At six months, a baby says 'da-da-da' and 'ma-ma-ma' without meaning anything by it. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Correct. Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.

questions.explanation: Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.

questions.stem: Without ever being taught, salmon swim back to the stream where they hatched in order to breed. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
Correct. Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.

questions.explanation: Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes fidelity?

options.text: The ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices
options.why: That describes respect for people's rights and dignity.

options.text: The ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate
options.why: That describes integrity.

options.text: The ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises
options.why: Correct. This is what fidelity means.

options.text: The ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm
options.why: That describes nonmaleficence.

questions.explanation: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight?

options.why: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.
Correct. Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.
Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.

questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of amusement

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of amusement.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Amusement was defined as the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that held the pen between the teeth rated the cartoons as funnier. On average, the value was 6.6 for the group that held the pen between the teeth and 5.1 for the group that held the pen between the lips, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 90 university students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that held the pen between the teeth rated the cartoons as funnier. (6.6 compared with 5.1).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the facial expression produced by holding a pen affects amusement. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the facial expression produced by holding a pen. The finding illustrates the facial-feedback hypothesis: facial expressions can influence the emotions people feel.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Long-term stress harms health, but coping strategies and social support reduce its effects.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, people with more stressful life events had more colds in the same year (r = +0.33).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the general adaptation syndrome: prolonged stress keeps the body in the resistance phase and eventually exhausts it, which suppresses the immune system and makes illness more likely.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers who practiced mindfulness meditation had lower cortisol levels (9.8) than workers who listened to an audiobook (13.5).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through emotion-focused coping: meditation manages the emotional and physical reaction to stress, which lowers the body's stress-hormone response.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
